1	# FZ v3 cloud build: quality log (2026-09-29)
2	
3	BRIEF addendum 5: the cloud run starts from scratch; `fz_v3/built/` (the local build under a 1 GB / 2-process limit) is a
4	cross-check only; a local number the cloud rebuild does not reproduce is discarded and recorded here.
5	
6	## Environment
7	
8	Cloud container: 4 cores, 15 GB RAM, no GPU. Python 3.11.15; numpy 2.4.6, pandas 3.0.6 (the local build used 2.3.3 on
9	Python 3.10), pyarrow 25.0.1, scipy 1.17.1, scikit-learn 1.9.1, xgboost 3.2.0, lightgbm 4.7.0, shap 0.51.0, numba 0.67.0,
10	statsmodels 0.15.0, hmmlearn 0.3.3, mapie 1.5.0, ruptures 1.1.10, arch 8.0.0, stumpy 1.14.1, torch 2.14.0 (CPU wheel; the
11	pytorch.org index is blocked by the proxy, PyPI served it), joblib 1.6.0, matplotlib 3.11.2, psutil 7.2.2. Every library the
12	design panel names is present, so nothing is hand-coded for lack of a package.
13	
14	## Build (`out/build/build.py`, one process per timeframe, `engine.load` on the full committed files)
15	
16	| | 1 minute | 5 minute |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| bars / sessions | 443,826 / 1,188 | 88,771 / 1,188 |
19	| first / last bar | 2021-10-01 09:15 / 2026-09-25 15:29 | 2021-10-01 09:15 / 2026-09-25 15:25 |
20	| front_month = 0 bars / zero-volume bars | 0 / 4 | 0 / 2 |
21	| engine.run wall time | 306 s (local box: 958 s) | 10 s (local: 51 s) |
22	| whole build, peak RSS | 351 s, 1.66 GB | 20 s, 0.54 GB |
23	| swings / events (CHoCH, BOS) | 130,843 / 39,608 (8,054, 31,554) | 26,578 / 7,950 (1,532, 6,418) |
24	| SETUPs = Foundation trades, engine-skipped | 5,326, 0 | 1,012, 0 |
25	| rooms / watches / ST7-ST8 positions (TAKE + REENTER) | 6,802 / 2,644 / 711 + 164 | 4,673 / 476 / 269 + 124 |
26	
27	## Cross-check against the local build (`out/build/compare.py`, `data/<tf>/compare.json`)
28	
29	**Identical on both timeframes:** the SETUP list, every Foundation trade (entry, exit bar, exit price, pts, charges, net, stop,
30	exit reason), every FZ position (entry, exit, pts, net, gate, room id, fill, reenter reason), the per-bar room card (zone, visit,
31	bars, read, left room, outside run, containing room, wick depth, touches, cluster sit, leave R4), every room (id, edges, birth,
32	retirement), the event list and the swing list. The local numbers in `built/*/README.md` and `meta.json` are therefore all
33	reproduced (IS 1m: 4,502 trades, net -4,150,085.95, 684 wins; 5m: 832, -230,262.16, 184; ST7 745 kept IS / 130 OOS, ST8 325 / 68),
34	and nothing from the local build is discarded.
35	
36	**Feature columns that differ, by definition (cloud definitions are the ones the studies use):**
37	- `range_1h/3h_atr` (local 5m `range12/36_atr`): the cloud windows stop at the session's first bar (157 / 378 of 1,012 rows differ,
38	  the ones whose window crossed the overnight gap in the local build).
39	- `hv3_*` (5m): the cloud baseline is the same-session median of the previous 20 bars with at least 5 of them (the local 5m build
40	  used a cross-session 20-bar median): 466 rows differ in `hv3_bars_since`, 600 in `hv3_dir`. The 1m `vol_hv*` columns (same
41	  definition as the cloud) are identical.
42	- `fnd_mfe_pts` / `fnd_mae_pts` (5m): the cloud follows `lab.excursion` (MFE >= 0, MAE <= 0); the local 5m build kept raw signs
43	  (1,008 MAE rows differ in sign, 7 MFE rows where the high never exceeded the entry). The 1m columns are identical.
44	- 1m `reg_range60_atr` and `reg_prior_closed_pts_today` have no cloud twin (`range_1h_atr` is same-session; `today_pts_asof` uses
45	  `exit <= k`, the same rule); every other shared 1m feature column is identical, including all `lvl_touch_*` verdicts and the
46	  `card_*` / `st7_*` (now `fz_*`) gate columns.
47	- New in the cloud table (not in either local table): the L1 label (`l1_*`), `n_choch_since_bos_today`, `alt_dir6` + `alt_kind6`,
48	  `er_1h`, `ret_1h/3h_pts`, `today_pts_asof`, `fz_pos_in_band_dir`, `fz_band_width_atr`, `fzpos_l1_*`.
49	
50	## Causality (`out/build/trunc_diff.py`, cut 2025-06-30 12:00:00, mid-session)
51	
52	The same build on the bars up to the cut against the full build: **PASS on both timeframes.** 1 minute: 335,934 bars, 3,807 SETUPs
53	at or before the cut, all 201 as-of columns identical, bars (atr14, protected level, volume baselines) and the whole room card
54	identical, swings / events / rooms as of the cut identical, the ledger's gate columns identical, the 3,806 closed trades identical;
55	only the `fnd_*` label columns of the trades still open at the cut differ. 5 minutes: 67,192 bars, 718 SETUPs, the same result.
56	So no as-of column depends on bars after the SETUP bar. Any extended feature a study adds must pass the same diff
57	(`data/<tf>/trunc_20250630_120000/` holds the truncated bars and tables for that).
58	
59	## The two labels (pre-registration, `results/pre_registration.json`)
60	
61	| IS book | 1m L0 (engine exit) | 1m L1 (15:25 cut) | 5m L0 | 5m L1 |
62	|---|---|---|---|---|
63	| units | 4,502 | 4,452 (50 SETUPs open at / after 15:25 not taken) | 832 | 826 |
64	| net INR / mean per trade | -4,150,086 / -922 | -4,494,773 / -1,010 | -230,262 / -277 | -625,325 / -757 |
65	| win rate | 15.2% | 15.6% | 22.1% | 27.7% |
66	| trades the cut changed | | 473 (`eod` 471, `expiry` 2) | | 289 (`eod` 280, `expiry` 9) |
67	| top-decile winners' share of gross wins | 57.9% | 44.7% | 45.5% | 31.3% |
68	| mean cost (charges + 650 slippage) | 1,048 | 1,048 | 1,050 | 1,050 |
69	
70	The 15:25 cut removes the overnight holds, which were the profitable part of the engine's book (S47), so the L1 book that
71	ST13/ST14 would trade is worse than the engine's, most on 5 minutes (-757 vs -277 per trade). Every gate is judged on L1 (the
72	book a `square_off 15:25` strategy trades) with L0 as the robustness table; this is stated on every OOS table.
73	
74	**The frozen ST7/ST8 gate on L1 (the comparator):** 1m kept 745 of 4,452 (16.7%), kept mean -1,026 vs skipped -1,006 (diff -20,
75	permutation p 0.85, session-matched control 62.6th percentile, loser recall 0.84 but it also skips 82% of the winners' net and
76	84% of the top-decile winners); 5m kept 325 of 826 (39%), kept mean -979 vs skipped -613 (diff -366, p 0.24, 13.6th percentile).
77	The frozen gate fails every go / no-go item except the kept-n floors: it is not a loser filter (H1 in `studies/h1_gate_audit`).
78	
79	**Break tests on the per-session L1 net (active IS sessions, 578 on 1m / 408 on 5m):** BDE CUSUM finds no break inside IS
80	(max band ratio 0.56 / 0.53); the HAC Chow tests per calendar year are all p > 0.14 except 5m 2023 (t -2.40, p 0.017: the 5m
81	book's mean per session fell from +631 to -498 in 2023); the IS / OOS boundary Chow test is p 0.63 (1m) / 0.56 (5m): no boundary
82	break at 5%, so OOS is read as the same process and no time-decay weighting is forced (the c = 0.5 variant is still reported as a
83	sensitivity in the meta-label study, as the design says).
84	
85	## Splitter (`harness.check_splits`)
86	
87	12 contiguous blocks of 85-86 IS sessions; IS rows per block 1m 170-512, 5m 31-83; purged training rows per block 0-29 (1m),
88	0-8 (5m); 66 CPCV splits; every IS row tested exactly once in the 12-block scheme; no training row's label lifetime intersects
89	its test block; no training row sits in the 3-session embargo (asserted).
90

1	# FZ v3 design panel (2026-09-29)
2	
3	Three designers (quant-ML canon, sequence / representation learning, decision-making / RL) proposed studies for the FZ v3 program; two judges (feasibility-and-rigour, skeptical practitioner) scored each on feasible_here / rigour / expected_value (0-5) with keep = all three >= 3. Generated from the workflow result; the judges' fixes are part of the program. Feasibility was scored against the local 4-core box; in the cloud the compute ceilings do not apply, the rigour and overfitting fixes do.
4	
5	## Scoreboard
6	
7	| id | lens priority | J1 feas/rig/ev keep | J2 feas/rig/ev keep |
8	|---|---|---|---|
9	| deep-sequence-llm-hypotheses | 1 | 5/3/3 KEEP | 5/3/3 KEEP |
10	| deep-sequence-regime-states | 2 | 4/4/2 drop | 4/4/3 KEEP |
11	| deep-sequence-rocket-probe | 3 | 3/3/2 drop | 3/4/2 drop |
12	| deep-sequence-vision-labels | 4 | 3/3/2 drop | 3/3/3 KEEP |
13	| deep-sequence-motif-shapelet | 5 | 4/3/1 drop | 4/4/2 drop |
14	| deep-sequence-pretrain-probe | 6 | 2/3/1 drop | 2/4/1 drop |
15	| quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo | 1 | 5/4/3 KEEP | 5/5/4 KEEP |
16	| quant-ml-canon-meta-label-gate | 2 | 5/4/3 KEEP | 5/4/4 KEEP |
17	| quant-ml-canon-feature-importance | 3 | 5/4/3 KEEP | 5/4/3 KEEP |
18	| quant-ml-canon-conformal-skip | 4 | 5/4/2 drop | 5/4/3 KEEP |
19	| quant-ml-canon-bet-sizing | 5 | 5/3/2 drop | 5/4/2 drop |
20	| quant-ml-canon-regime-breaks | 6 | 4/4/2 drop | 5/4/3 KEEP |
21	| decision-making-1-fullinfo-bandit-policy-tree-gate | 1 | 5/4/3 KEEP | 5/4/4 KEEP |
22	| decision-making-2-exit-policy-fqi-exomdp | 2 | 2/4/3 drop | 3/4/3 KEEP |
23	| decision-making-3-robustness-resampling-multiplicity-adversarial | 3 | 4/4/3 KEEP | 3/4/3 KEEP |
24	| decision-making-4-selective-gate-conformal-risk-control | 4 | 5/4/2 drop | 5/4/3 KEEP |
25	| decision-making-5-kelly-bounded-sizing | 5 | 5/3/1 drop | 5/4/2 drop |
26	| decision-making-6-session-stop-rule-finite-horizon | 6 | 5/4/3 KEEP | 5/5/3 KEEP |
27	
28	## Judges' verdicts
29	
30	### Judge 1
31	
32	Skeptical-practitioner verdict. The tape sets the ceiling before any model runs: 1m Foundation is +1.9 pts per trade gross against ~16 pts of cost (mean net -922 INR, 15.2% winners, 4,502 IS SETUPs in 579 active sessions); 5m is 184 IS winners with the top decile carrying ~46% of gross and an IS-to-OOS mean shift from -277 to -1,060 per trade. So any gate must find a subset whose expectancy clears ~16-20 pts, and the whole signal lives in a few hundred trades on 1m and a few dozen on 5m. On that sample the block-bootstrap CI of a kept-vs-skipped difference will be several hundred INR per trade wide; most candidates will not clear it, and that is the honest expected outcome. Every library the 18 studies name is present (sklearn 1.7.2 with interaction_cst/monotonic_cst, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, pyarrow, scipy, matplotlib) and statsmodels/torch/mapie are absent as assumed; feasibility failures are compute and memory, not imports.
33	
34	Keep seven, merged into five lines of work, about 1-1.5 CPU-hours per timeframe in total: (1) one validation harness = quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo with decision-making-3's SPA, adversarial drift and 5m null tapes folded in (one ledger, one bootstrap, one PBO, active sessions only, every comparator re-priced on the L1 15:25 label); (2) one feature-vocabulary pass = quant-ml-canon-feature-importance, its 8-cluster shortlist frozen in the ledger before any gate search, with BOCPD, FFD and the novelty scalars entering there and nowhere else; (3) one learned-gate family = quant-ml-canon-meta-label-gate and decision-making-1 merged (L1 label, capped |net| weights, top-1%-winners-removed as a hard pass, block-wise sign test, one distilled rule list or scorecard as the single OOS candidate from the family); (4) the interpretable candidate = deep-sequence-llm-hypotheses with a blind round 0 from the user's words alone, hashed before any table is shown, and cross-fitted round-1 tables; (5) the cheap desk rule = decision-making-6 session stop with an hour-conditioned null. That yields at most three OOS looks: the rule list from (3), the round-0 list from (4), and the frozen ST7/ST8 gate as comparator, with (5) as a multiplication if its null is rejected.
35	
36	Drop or defer eleven. The sequence and representation studies (rocket, pretrain, HMM/jump, motif/shapelet, vision) share one structural flaw: the only shippable form is a depth-3 tree on the same scalar features the tabular studies already search, so they add trials to the ledger without adding a candidate, and the pre-SETUP window is templated by the engine's own SETUP definition; pretrain and 1m FQI also need 750-900 MB for hours on a box shared with another build. The two conformal studies and the two sizing studies do not change which SETUPs are taken: they choose a threshold on a score another study produces, or size a positive edge that does not yet exist; their useful pieces (slippage 3/5/8 sensitivity, Pareto front with user-chosen w, |net|-weighted coverage, one-lot-or-skip verdict) become sections of the gate study's deliverable. The regime-breaks study keeps only its break tests as the harness's pre-registration step (they decide time-decay weights and the OOS caveat); BSADF is a feature candidate for the importance pass, not a gate. The exit study is worth its parametric learner C (config keys the lab already has, 10 minutes by replay) but must be coordinated with the ST9-12 session, which already ran an exit grid on 2026.
37	
38	Two standing caveats every OOS table must carry: the OOS window (2026-01-01..09-25) is also the published lab dashboard window and was used by the ST9-12 exit grid, so it is not pristine; and the 5m Foundation label as built holds 358 of 1,012 trades past the entry session, so ST13/ST14 (square_off 15:25) must be judged on the recomputed intraday label and every comparator re-priced on it.
39	
40	### Judge 2
41	
42	Twelve of eighteen studies are worth running here; six are cut or folded. The binding facts: (1) sample size, not compute, is the limit: 684 IS winners on 1m and 184 on 5m, a 15-22% win rate, mean net -922 INR per trade against ~1,050 INR costs, so a gate must find a subset averaging > 16 pts, and the top-decile winners are half of gross wins; every learned number must therefore be reported as a CPCV path distribution (5th percentile), with |net| weights winsorised and kept-n floors. (2) memory: lab.py holds 1.24 GB and 759 MB is free, so the '2 processes under 1 GB' budget is currently one process under ~600 MB; the rocket probe at 10k kernels, the pretrain ladder, 1m FQI and 1m synthetic tapes do not fit until lab.py exits. (3) libraries: everything named that is present imports (numpy, pandas, scipy, sklearn 1.7.2 with interaction_cst/monotonic_cst, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, pyarrow, matplotlib, PIL, joblib); statsmodels, torch, mapie, hmmlearn, ruptures, arch are absent and every study that names them correctly hand-codes. Structural fixes that apply across the set: there must be ONE harness (merge quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo with decision-making-3's bootstrap/PBO): 12 contiguous IS session blocks, purge by the label's own exit bar, 3-session embargo, one append-only ledger reached only through a score() function, PBO <= 0.2, kept-share/kept-n floors, slippage-8-pt survival, and ONE OOS script run once for at most 3 frozen candidates; all eighteen 'OOS once' clauses collapse into that, otherwise OOS is opened eighteen times. Four near-duplicate pairs merge: meta-label + policy-tree gate (the central study, EV 4), conformal-skip + conformal-risk-control (one operating-point step the user chooses on), the two sizing studies (conditional on a gate surviving; prior is 'one lot or skip'), the two harnesses. The L1 intraday (15:25) label written once is the only training label; the engine label's multi-session holds (358 of 1,012 on 5m) make purging by it too costly. Regime, novelty and state-model outputs enter as candidate features into the importance study rather than as separate gate searches, which is the cheapest cut in multiplicity. The LLM-hypothesis study needs a blind round 0 and a trials count equal to the labelled cells shown; the vision study runs as a 40-session pilot against mechanical proxies first; both must be separate agents from any study author. Cut: pretrain-probe (3-4 h, 750 MB, negative result foreseen), motif/shapelet (keep only the causal novelty score), rocket as proposed (reduce to a 5-minute ceiling check), both sizing studies as standalone. Run order: break tests and L1 label, harness, importance, merged gate, operating point, exit learners C and B (FQI on 5m only), session-stop, BOCPD/GMM regime, LLM rounds, vision pilot, null tapes on 5m; everything above 600 MB waits for lab.py.
43	
44	## Designers' rationales
45	
46	- What this lens can honestly do on this box. The brief's data now exists in the session scratchpad (fz_v3/5minute complete; fz_v3/minute engine/trades written, features running): 5m has 1,012 Foundation SETUPs (832 IS / 180 OOS, 22% net winners, mean net -277 INR), 1m has 5,326 (4,502 IS / 824 OOS, 15% winners, mean net -922 INR, sd ~5,300 INR, median hold 15 bars, p90 92). So the supervised sample is 4.5k rows with ~680 positive labels on 1m and 830 rows with 184 positives on 5m; OOS confirmation rests on 128 and 37 winners respectively. Standard error of an OOS mean net is ~185 INR/trade (1m) and ~375 INR/trade (5m): a gate must move kept-vs-skipped expectancy by roughly 500 (1m) / 1,000 (5m) INR per trade to be visible at all, and nothing subtler is decidable on this tape. Every study below is sized to that reality: the models are feature extractors and regime detectors whose output is distilled into a compact rule list, not end-to-end deep classifiers.
47	
48	Library reality, checked with `python -c import`: torch, tensorflow, hmmlearn, stumpy, ruptures, tslearn, sktime, pyts are absent and nothing may be installed. Present: numpy 2.2, sklearn 1.7.2, pandas 2.3, scipy 1.14, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2, shap 0.49, matplotlib 3.9, PIL, pyarrow, psutil. Consequences, stated per study: a gradient-trained 1D-CNN/GRU/Transformer is not possible without a framework (a hand-written numpy CNN is a day of build for no expected gain at n=4.5k); its honest modern substitute is the random-convolutional-kernel transform (ROCKET/MiniRocket) plus a linear probe, which the literature shows matches small CNNs on small time-series benchmarks and which I benchmarked here at 2.1 s per 1,500 windows x 2,000 kernels. Contrastive pretraining (InfoNCE) needs a custom loss, so the self-supervised study uses the ladder PCA -> sklearn MLP autoencoder -> forecast-pretext encoder and reports whether anything beats PCA. Matrix profile, HMM, statistical jump model and Bayesian online change-point detection are all implementable in numpy/numba in under 150 lines each and were timed (FFT distance profile 0.19 s per query over the whole 445k-bar 1m tape; GMM on 90k x 6 in 51 s).
49	
50	Machine: 4 cores, 7.9 GB total but only ~0.9 GB free at the time of writing (lab.py rebuild holds 1.5 GB, the 1m feature build ~200 MB), so studies must run one at a time until the rebuild finishes, and every study is designed to peak under 800 MB with 1m windows stored as float32 and never more than ~150k pretraining windows in memory at once.
51	
52	Common protocol shared by all six (each study's leakage_controls field adds the study-specific parts): (1) unit = Foundation SETUP with its own engine trade from the build (fnd_net_inr, fnd_win, exit reason); (2) every feature/window uses bars <= setup_i (the SETUP bar's close is the entry; the window ends at k inclusive); (3) IS-only learning with purged, embargoed, session-blocked CV: 5 contiguous chronological blocks of ~205 IS sessions, training SETUPs whose Foundation exit session falls in the test block or its embargo are purged, embargo = max sessions_held observed on that timeframe (+1), all normalisation/PCA/kernel-bias/model parameters fit inside the training folds; (4) OOS (2026-01-01..2026-09-25) is scored once by a single logged script run with the model frozen on all IS, never re-tuned; (5) judgement is kept-vs-skipped mean-net difference with fz_report.permutation_p, the session-matched random control percentile (fz_report.random_control; the current ST7/ST8 sit at the 39.6th/57th percentile, so the bar is 'above the 95th'), precision/recall on losers, and the share of top-decile winners skipped; net alone is never the criterion because every gate that trades less banks ~1,114 INR per skipped 1m trade; (6) multiplicity: every configuration tried is counted and a max-T permutation across the family (White's Reality Check style) is reported next to the single-rule p; (7) output = a candidate ST13/ST14 gate block: <= 8 conjunctive rules of depth <= 3 over named as-of features with provenance 'learned on IS 2021-10..2025-12, script <name>, sha'; any non-scalar artefact (HMM parameters, a shapelet template) is offered only as an alternative that needs a user decision on a new fz key and code contract.
53	
54	Ordering: the LLM-hypothesis study is first because it is config-native, cheap and directly encodes the user's own reads; the regime-state study second because 'sideways hurts' is the user's central claim and the models are small enough to ship; the random-kernel probe third as the cheapest ceiling test for 'is there information in the bar shape at all'; vision labels fourth because they give the user's visual notion of sideways a ground truth (and the first number, Foundation expectancy by hindsight label, decides whether any causal detector is worth building); motif/shapelet fifth; self-supervised pretraining last because without a framework it is the most likely to report 'nothing beyond PCA'. Sizing and exits: studies 2 and 3 emit a per-SETUP expectancy score; the brief's exits stay Foundation's, so sizing appears only as a secondary output (lots 0/1/2 by score tercile) judged with the same control; a during-trade version of the window models for early exits is a natural follow-on once the position-path table exists, and is not proposed here.
55	
56	- Lens and framing. Foundation is the primary model: it fixes side, entry bar and exit rule for every SETUP, and (decisively) its outcome is observed for every SETUP in the data, taken or not. So the take/skip/size decision at the SETUP bar is a one-step problem with full-information feedback: it is supervised meta-labelling in Lopez de Prado's sense, not a bandit (no off-policy correction is needed because the counterfactual is in the table) and not sequential RL (no position overlap: 0 of 1,003 Foundation trades overlap on 5m, by construction the next SETUP needs the CHoCH that exits the previous trade). Everything proposed below descends from that framing: the labels and weights (AFML ch. 3-4), the validation harness (ch. 7, 11-14), importance with substitution effects removed (ch. 8; MLAM ch. 6), calibrated sizing (ch. 10), conformal sets for the skip decision (Vovk; Angelopoulos and Bates), and break/explosiveness statistics as regime features (ch. 17). Sample-size reality drives the design: on 5m IS there are 823 SETUPs and 181 winners; the engine-label net has std 10,271 INR (holds run to 70 sessions because the engine has no square-off), so a kept-vs-skipped expectancy difference below about 1,400 INR per trade (400 vs 400 split, 5% two-sided) is undetectable on that label. The intraday label (exit forced at the entry session's 15:25 bar, the lab's ST1/ST2 book) is therefore the primary label in every study; the top decile of winners carries 46% of gross wins (win mean +10,878, loss mean -3,429), so every gate is judged on |net|-weighted winner recall and kept-vs-skipped expectancy plus the session-matched random control, never on accuracy or net alone (a gate that trades less always saves costs). Data facts the studies rely on: the 5-minute table at scratchpad/fz_v3/5minute (features.parquet, 186 columns, 143 as-of; 97 numeric with 114 pairs |rho| > 0.9; causality verified by the truncated build), the 1-minute table not yet landed (scripts 01-03 only) but promised with the same column contract (a few thousand SETUPs). Box: 4 logical cores, 7.9 GB RAM with about 1.2 GB free beside the other session's 1.1 GB lab process; every study is a single process under 500 MB and 25 CPU-minutes per timeframe, at most two at a time, no pip installs (numpy 2.2.6, sklearn 1.7.2, pandas 2.3.3, scipy 1.14.1, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, numba 0.65, joblib; statsmodels/mapie/mlfinlab/lightgbm/torch absent, so ADF, CUSUM, FFD, conformal and PBO are hand-coded in numpy, all short). Order and dependencies: the harness (study 2) first because every other study and H1-H5 consume its splitter and trials ledger; then meta-labelling (1) which also hands H5 its labels, weights, OOF probabilities and splitter instead of a second gradient-boosting run; importance (3) and regime (6) can run in parallel with (1) since they only need the splitter; conformal (4) and sizing (5) consume (1)'s OOF file and are cheap. Deliberately left out with reasons: sequential bootstrap (uniqueness is 1 by construction for Foundation labels; only the triple-barrier variants with vertical barriers overlap and those get the concurrency weights inside study 1); HRP / portfolio construction (one instrument); deep sequence models and transformers (1k-5k labels, no GPU, and nothing to distil into 8 rules); sequential RL (one-step decision with the counterfactual observed); generative AI in the LLM sense (no standing in the canon at this sample size; the only generative element the canon endorses here is the CPCV path distribution and the stationary block bootstrap of sessions in study 2, which is what gives the confidence intervals). OOS discipline shared by all six: candidate configs and the exact scoring scripts are frozen to JSON with a sha before any OOS row is read; the harness pre-registers the go/no-go rule (PBO <= 0.2, CPCV 5th-percentile kept-vs-skipped difference > 0, deflated-Sharpe p < 0.1, at most three candidates across all lenses get the one OOS look); the frozen ST7/ST8 gate is always one of the comparators; ST13/ST14 must carry square_off "15:25" so that the traded book matches the label the gate was learned on.
57	
58	- Why this lens splits the problem the way it does. (1) The take/skip choice at a Foundation SETUP is a contextual bandit with FULL information: Foundation took every SETUP, so the reward of "take" (fnd_net, 1m: 5,326 rows, 5m: 1,012 rows) is logged for every context, and the reward of "skip" is exactly 0 by definition. There is no unobserved arm, hence no propensity model, no inverse-propensity weighting and no doubly-robust correction: the off-policy value of ANY gate pi is computed exactly as sum over SETUPs of pi(x)*net(x). The only statistical problem is generalisation from a few thousand contexts, so the right tools are cost-sensitive policy learning (value-maximising policy trees, cost-proportionate weighting) and honest selection, not bandit exploration. (2) Sequential RL is genuinely justified only where today's action changes which future rewards remain reachable: the in-trade exit (hold/exit/partial each bar; 1m IS has ~186k intraday bar-steps inside positions, ~800k once trajectories are extended to the 15:25 square-off) and, at session level, whether to keep trading today. On a price-taker's tape the dynamics are exogenous (an Exo-MDP): any exit policy can be replayed exactly and the hindsight-optimal exit is computable per trade, so OPE (DR/MAGIC) is not the bottleneck; generalisation and multiplicity are. Deep offline RL (CQL, IQL, Decision Transformer) and neural generators (TimeGAN, diffusion) are not runnable here (no torch) and would be badly over-parameterised for 4.5k trajectories anyway; the studies say so and use the closest feasible analogues (pessimistic tree-ensemble FQI, hindsight-imitation, GMM-Markov and session-bootstrap tapes). (3) Sizing is a downstream Kelly problem that only exists once a positive-conditional-edge region is found; the raw book (win rate 15%, mean -922 INR) has negative Kelly, and the study is written to return "0 lots" honestly. (4) Costs are 1,050-1,120 INR per trade and the median 1m trade moves 9 pts, so a gate that trades less always raises net by the saved costs: every study judges on kept-vs-skipped expectancy, the session-matched random control at the same per-session position count (fz_report.random_control), the permutation p, and (new here) the multiplicity-adjusted SPA/PBO from session-block resampling. (5) Leakage discipline is shared: features from the as-of columns only (prefixes fnd_, fwd_, fzpos_, st7_ POST columns, swings.broken_final, events.window_end/end, zones/visits final-state fields are excluded), contiguous session-block CV with purge (drop training trades whose exit falls in the test block) and a 2-session embargo, OOS (2026-01-01..2026-09-25) touched once per study at the end; the 5-minute engine trades are re-cut at 15:25 from bars because the build carries no square-off (358 of 1,012 held overnight). Priority order: the gate (1), the exit policy (2), then the robustness/multiplicity certificate that must pass before any key ships (3), the certified operating point (4), sizing (5), the session-stop rule (6). Compute: every study fits in one process under 1 GB; the two heavy jobs (1m FQI ensemble, 1m synthetic tapes) must not run concurrently with each other because each peaks near 900 MB.
59	
60	## Studies
61	
62	### deep-sequence-llm-hypotheses (priority 1)
63	
64	**technique.** LLM-as-hypothesis-generator with pre-registration and a family-wise permutation test: Claude reads IS-only summaries of the per-SETUP feature table and writes a fixed, hashed list of candidate skip rules before any rule is scored.
65	
66	**what_it_answers.** Does a small set of human-readable rules, written from the user's own observations (sideways after repeated CHoCH, reaction to visibly high volume, respected vs broken levels, time of day, room read) plus what the IS marginals show, skip losers without skipping winners; and is the effect real after correcting for having proposed several rules at once? 84	### deep-sequence-regime-states (priority 2)
85	
86	**technique.** Latent regime states from per-bar features: a hand-rolled Gaussian HMM (Baum-Welch, causal forward filtering at inference), a statistical jump model (k-means with a jump penalty, online prefix version), a GaussianMixture no-dynamics baseline, and Bayesian online change-point detection (BOCPD) run-length features; all fit on IS bars only.
87	
88	**what_it_answers.** Is there a machine-found 'chop' state that marks losing Foundation SETUPs better than the hand rule H2 tests (n_choch_since_bos >= k), how many bars of confirmation it needs (the filtered state lags), and whether 'time since the last structural change' (BOCPD run length) carries the same information more cheaply. Also gives the vision study (below) a mechanical comparator.
89	
90	**method.** Per-bar as-of feature vector x_t from fz_v3/<tf>/bars.csv and events.csv: |log return|, (high-low)/atr14, |close-open|/(high-low), log(volume/median volume of the previous 20 bars), events (BOS+CHoCH) in the last 36 bars, CHoCHs since the last BOS at t, range of the last 36 bars / atr14, signed 36-bar return / atr14; features are z-scored with IS statistics. Models: (a) Gaussian HMM with K in {3,4}, diagonal covariance, Baum-Welch 50 iterations in numba, initialised from k-means, fit on IS bars of the training folds; at inference only the forward (filtered) posterior P(s_t | x_<=t) is used; the smoothed posterior is computed too but only as a hindsight diagnostic. (b) Statistical jump model: minimise sum ||x_t - mu_{s_t}||^2 + lambda * 1[s_t != s_{t-1}] by alternating centroid updates and Viterbi DP, lambda from a small grid chosen on CV; the online state is the prefix-DP argmax. (c) sklearn GaussianMixture(K) on the same vectors as the no-dynamics baseline. (d) BOCPD (Adams & MacKay) with a normal-inverse-gamma predictive on 1m/5m log returns and separately on log range, hazard 1/H for H in {60, 240} bars, run-length truncated at 400; features: MAP run length, P(run length < 10), bars since the last MAP reset. At each SETUP bar k the study attaches: P(state = c | x_<=k) for each state, the jump-model state, and the BOCPD features. Analysis: Foundation net and win rate by filtered state and by BOCPD run-length bucket on IS; identify the state with the worst expectancy (the candidate chop state) inside each training fold; gate = skip when P(chop) >= tau (tau grid 0.5..0.9) or run length >= r; evaluate on purged session-blocked CV against H2's rule at matched skip fraction (the HMM must beat the hand rule's kept-vs-skipped difference at the same trade count, else it is not worth its parameters); final model refit on all IS; OOS once. Outputs: state description tables (means per feature), transition matrix, the expectancy-by-state table on IS CV and OOS, the control percentile, and the distilled rule.
91	
92	**leakage_controls.** Only filtered (forward) posteriors and prefix-DP states are used at SETUP bars; smoothed posteriors and full-sequence Viterbi paths are labelled hindsight and never enter a feature; all model parameters and z-scoring statistics are estimated on IS training-fold bars only, refit per fold; BOCPD is causal by construction; the chop state is identified per training fold, not on the test fold; embargo covers the longest Foundation hold; OOS bars are only ever filtered through the frozen IS model.
93	
94	**compute.** 5m: HMM 76k bars x 8 features x 4 states x 50 EM iterations in numba ~1 min per fold, 5 folds ~5 min; 1m 445k bars ~5 min per fold, ~25 min; jump model similar; GMM ~1 min per fit (benchmarked 51 s for 90k x 6 x 4 components); BOCPD 445k x 400 run lengths in numba ~1 min. Total ~40-60 CPU-minutes per timeframe; peak memory under 400 MB (bars as float32, per-bar posteriors K x N float32).
95	
96	**libraries.** numpy, numba (HMM forward/backward, jump-model DP, BOCPD), sklearn.mixture.GaussianMixture and sklearn.cluster.KMeans for initialisation, pandas.
97	
98	**output_as_config.** Preferred: a distilled rule list over scalar as-of features that reproduces the chop-state gate (a depth-3 tree fit to predict 'P(chop) >= tau' from the same per-bar features must reach >= 85% fidelity on CV, else the study says the state is not expressible compactly). Alternative needing a user decision: an fz block key such as {"regime": {"model": "hmm_filtered", "features": [...], "means": [[...]], "vars": [[...]], "transition": [[...]], "chop_state": 2, "skip_if_p_chop_ge": 0.7}} (about 40-60 numbers for K=4 x 8 features) plus a forward-filter routine in fz code; the BOCPD variant is two numbers (hazard, run-length threshold) and is compact by itself.
99	
100	**novelty.** Markov-switching regimes (Hamilton 1989) and Gaussian HMMs (Rabiner 1989) are classical; the current pieces are statistical jump models for regime detection with an online variant (Bemporad et al. 2018; Nystrup, Kolm & Lindstrom 2020/2021, 'sparse jump models'), Bayesian online change-point detection (Adams & MacKay 2007) as a causal alternative to offline change-point search (ruptures, Truong et al. 2020), and the discipline of separating filtered from smoothed states (the look-ahead trap in regime backtests documented by Nystrup et al.).
101	
102	**Judge 1** feasible 4 · rigour 4 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: Trap: a Gaussian HMM on |return|, range/ATR and event counts finds volatility states, not the user's chop; the 'worst-expectancy state' is picked per fold from K states (label switching plus selection), the filtered posterior lags 10-30 bars at 1m, and the only shippable form is a depth-3 tree on the same scalar features, at which point the HMM added nothing but trials. Fix: run only BOCPD (two numbers, causal, one minute) and hand run-length features to study 3; run the HMM only if study 3 shows the H2 counts are not already the regime cluster, and then on 5m only.
103	
104	**Judge 2** feasible 4 · rigour 4 · expected value 3 · keep True — fix: hmmlearn is absent, so Baum-Welch with scaling is hand-coded in numba (~150 lines, real bug risk): run the cheap rungs first, BOCPD (2-number config, numba, ~1 min) and sklearn GaussianMixture (benchmarked 51 s), and fit the HMM/jump model only if the GMM state already shows a kept-vs-skipped signal at matched skip fraction versus n_choch_since_bos on CV. Emit the state posteriors and BOCPD run length as candidate features to the importance study rather than running an own tau grid. The 40-60-number HMM config plus a forward filter in fz code is a new key type: record it as a user decision and ship only the distilled rule if fidelity >= 85%. 1m HMM is ~25 min per model set at < 400 MB, acceptable now; 5m first.

106	### deep-sequence-rocket-probe (priority 3)
107	
108	**technique.** Random convolutional kernel transform (MiniRocket-style: thousands of fixed dilated 1D kernels, proportion-of-positive-values pooling) over the multichannel pre-SETUP bar window, then a ridge/logistic linear probe; compared with an sklearn MLP on the same window and with the H5 tabular gradient-boosting reference; then distilled to rules.
109	
110	**what_it_answers.** Whether the shape of the last 60-120 bars (1m) / 12-36 bars (5m) before a SETUP carries any information about the Foundation outcome beyond the hand-built as-of features; how large the ceiling is (AUC and kept-vs-skipped expectancy at fixed skip fractions); and whether the part that matters can be written as a few threshold rules on scalar features.
111	
112	**method.** Window tensor per SETUP: L bars ending at setup_i inclusive (1m: L in {60, 120}; 5m: L in {12, 36}), channels: sg x log return per bar (direction-normalised so up and down SETUPs pool), (high-low)/atr14[k], sg x (close-open)/atr14[k], log(volume/vol_med20[k]) with NA -> 0 plus an NA flag channel, sg x (close - choch_lvl)/atr14[k], and a same-session indicator; stored float32. Transform: 5,000-10,000 random kernels of length 9, weights in {-1, 2} centred, dilations sampled log-uniformly up to L/4, one channel or a random pair per kernel, bias drawn from quantiles of the training-fold convolution outputs (as MiniRocket does), PPV pooling (numba, benchmarked 2.1 s per 1,500 windows x 2,000 kernels x 60 bars). Probes: RidgeClassifierCV on the PPV features (alpha grid 1e-3..1e3), L2 logistic regression for calibrated probabilities, and ridge regression on winsorised net (+-10,000 INR). Comparators inside the same CV folds: sklearn MLPClassifier(64,16) on the flattened z-scored window, H5's xgboost on tabular as-of features, and the stacked model (tabular + top PCA components of the PPV features). Selection on 5-fold purged session-blocked IS CV by: AUC, mean net of the kept set at skip fractions 30/50/70%, kept-vs-skipped difference, and the pooled session-matched control percentile of the kept set; incremental value = stacked minus tabular. Distillation: the probe score's bottom tercile ('predicted loser') becomes a binary target and a depth-3 decision tree on scalar as-of features (tabular + a handful of window summaries such as the sign-agreement count of the last 10 bars, the drawdown from the window high, the bar-range trend) is fit to it; the tree's rules are the config candidate if fidelity >= 85% and the rule's own CV kept-vs-skipped difference keeps >= 70% of the probe's. Final: refit on all IS, one OOS run. Outputs: the CV/OOS table for each model, calibration plot data, the distilled rules, and the statement of how much of the effect the rules keep.
113	
114	**leakage_controls.** Windows end at the SETUP bar; kernel biases, channel scaling and PCA are fit on training folds only, inside the CV loop; labels (fnd_net_inr) never enter the transform; purged/embargoed session-blocked CV; the number of window lengths x kernel counts x probes tried is recorded and a max-T permutation over that family is reported; OOS once with the frozen kernel set (seeds logged) and frozen ridge weights. Direction-normalisation is stated per channel so that no channel silently encodes a forward quantity.
115	
116	**compute.** Transform: 5,326 windows x 6 channels x 120 bars x 10,000 kernels ~90 s (+21 s JIT) per fold-fit of biases; RidgeCV on 5,326 x 10,000 ~2-5 min per fit; 5 folds x 2 window lengths x 3 probes ~45-75 CPU-minutes for 1m, ~10 min for 5m; MLP comparator ~5 min. Peak memory ~600 MB (feature matrix 5,326 x 10,000 float32 = 213 MB, doubled by sklearn's float64 copy; use 5,000 kernels if the lab rebuild is still holding memory).
117	
118	**libraries.** numpy, numba (kernel transform), sklearn (RidgeClassifierCV, LogisticRegression, MLPClassifier, DecisionTreeClassifier, PCA), xgboost for the H5 comparator, shap optional for the stacked model's attribution.
119	
120	**output_as_config.** Only the distilled rule list is proposed for ST13/ST14 (<= 8 rules of depth <= 3 over as-of scalar features, provenance 'distilled from rocket probe, script deep_rocket.py, sha'); the kernel bank and ridge weights (~10k numbers) are not compact and are explicitly not offered as config. If the probe shows a ceiling the rules cannot reach, the study reports the gap in INR/trade and stops.
121	
122	**novelty.** ROCKET (Dempster, Petitjean & Webb, DMKD 2020), MiniRocket (KDD 2021), MultiRocket (2022) and Hydra (2023) are the current state of the art for small-data time-series classification on CPU and descend from random-feature methods (Rahimi & Recht 2007) and untrained convolutional features; the linear-probe evaluation protocol is SimCLR's (Chen et al. 2020). It is the honest substitute for a gradient-trained 1D-CNN/GRU/Transformer on a box with no deep-learning framework and 4.5k labelled sequences.
123	
124	**Judge 1** feasible 3 · rigour 3 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: Trap: RidgeClassifierCV picks alpha by an internal leave-one-out that is not session-blocked, so 10,000 PPV features on ~3,600 windows fit within-session neighbours; every pre-SETUP window is templated by the engine's own SETUP definition (CHoCH then continuation), so shape 'motifs' are the rule, not information; the shippable form is again a scalar-feature tree, so at best it reports an unreachable ceiling. 125	
126	**Judge 2** feasible 3 · rigour 4 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: As proposed (10,000 kernels, 5,326 x 10,000 float32 doubled to float64 by RidgeCV, ~600 MB peak, 45-75 CPU-min) it does not fit beside lab.py at 1.24 GB with 759 MB free, and the prior that 4.5k labelled 60-bar windows beat hand features in intraday index futures is low. The distilled window summaries (sign-agreement count, drawdown from window high) can still be offered to the importance study as scalar features.

128	### deep-sequence-vision-labels (priority 4)
129	
130	**technique.** Multimodal Claude as a hindsight annotator: rendered IS session charts labelled sideways / trending per hour-bin by vision, with a reliability check; the labels are ground truth for (a) a direct test that sideways hurts Foundation SETUPs and (b) a causal detector distilled into rules.
131	
132	**what_it_answers.** Whether the user's visual notion of 'sideways' (the one behind 'CHoCH and CHoCH and no breaks') actually marks losing SETUPs on this tape; whether that notion is already captured by mechanical proxies (H2 counts, range/ATR, the HMM chop state) or adds something; and whether a causal detector can see it early enough to skip the trade.
133	
134	**method.** Rendering (deep_vision_render.py, matplotlib): for a stratified sample of 240 IS sessions (by year and by Foundation session net tercile so both good and bad sessions are present), a 1400x500 PNG of 5-minute candles with a volume panel, hour gridlines at 10:15/11:15/12:15/13:15/14:15 and a price axis; no date, no engine markers, filenames are opaque ids (the map id -> date is kept in a file the labeller does not read). Labelling: Claude reads each image via the Read tool and returns JSON with one label per hour-bin (SIDEWAYS / TREND_UP / TREND_DOWN / MIXED) and one session label; 40 images are re-labelled in a second pass in a different order for Cohen's kappa; a second variant with engine CHoCH/BOS markers drawn is labelled for a further 60 sessions to test whether the markers change the verdict. Reliability gate: kappa < 0.5 stops the study with that finding. Analysis A (the cheap decisive number): Foundation net and win rate of IS SETUPs by the hindsight label of their hour-bin and of the next hour-bin; permutation p; also the same by mechanical hindsight proxies (hour-bin range/ATR, |net move|/range) and their agreement with the vision labels (if a proxy reproduces the label at >= 90% the vision step is redundant and the proxy is used as the target instead). Extension to the whole IS: the detector's target for unlabelled sessions is the best mechanical proxy only if step A showed it agrees with vision at >= 90%; otherwise the detector is trained on the 240 labelled sessions only (about 1,000-1,200 SETUPs on 1m, ~200 on 5m) and that smaller n is stated. 138	**compute.** Rendering 300 charts ~3 CPU-minutes; detector training seconds; peak memory under 300 MB. 150	### deep-sequence-motif-shapelet (priority 5)
151	
152	**technique.** SETUP-anchored matrix-profile motif discovery (MASS/FFT z-normalised distances), time-series clustering of pre-SETUP shapes (k-means on z-normalised windows and on random-kernel features), and discriminative shapelet search; plus a causal novelty score (distance of the pre-SETUP window to the nearest earlier window on the tape).
153	
154	**what_it_answers.** Whether recurring pre-SETUP shapes exist (motifs), whether any motif or cluster has a Foundation expectancy that survives a session-blocked permutation test, whether a single short template (a shapelet) with a distance threshold separates losers, and whether 'this looks like nothing seen before' (novelty) or 'this looks exactly like a familiar pattern' predicts the outcome.
155	
156	**method.** Windows: the direction-normalised close path over the last m bars ending at setup_i (1m: m in {30, 60}; 5m: m in {12, 24}), z-normalised per window; a second representation is the 6-channel tensor of the rocket study. Motifs (deep_motif.py): full pairwise z-normalised Euclidean distance matrix among IS SETUP windows (4,502^2 x 60, seconds via matmul), nearest-neighbour graph, motif chains and agglomerative clustering with a distance cut chosen by the silhouette on training folds; per-cluster Foundation net, win rate, n, and a permutation p where the null shuffles labels within session blocks; clusters with n < 40 are reported but never proposed. Clustering (deep_cluster.py): k-means (k in 4..12) on the z-normalised paths and separately on the PPV features; cluster expectancy tables on CV (the cluster assignment for a test-fold SETUP uses training-fold centroids only); 'loser clusters' are then explained by a depth-3 tree on scalar as-of features (fidelity reported). Shapelets (deep_shapelet.py, numba): 3,000 random candidate subsequences of length 8-20 drawn from training-fold windows; for each, the minimum sliding distance to every window; information gain on fnd_win and the best threshold; the top 20 by gain re-scored on the held-out fold; a shapelet survives if its gain rank is stable across folds and its skip rule has kept-vs-skipped difference > 0 in every fold. Novelty (deep_novelty.py): for each SETUP the MASS distance profile of its m-bar window against the tape strictly before k - m (prefix only, so causal), taking the 1st-percentile distance and the nearest-neighbour distance as scalar features nn_dist_prefix, p1_dist_prefix; their deciles vs Foundation net; they are handed to the rule search of the LLM/H5 studies as candidate scalar features. All selection on purged session-blocked IS CV; family-wise p across every cluster/shapelet/threshold examined; OOS scored once with the frozen motif library, centroids and shapelets from all IS.
157	
158	**leakage_controls.** Windows end at the SETUP bar; the motif library, centroids and shapelets are built from training folds only inside CV and from all IS for the OOS run (a test window is never a member of the library it is scored against); the novelty score uses the tape prefix strictly before the window (bars <= k - m), never the future; cluster/shapelet counts examined are logged for the family-wise correction; small clusters are excluded from proposals; embargo/purge as in the common protocol; OOS once.
159	
160	**compute.** Pairwise distances seconds; k-means ~1 s per fit (benchmarked); shapelet search 3,000 candidates x 5,326 windows x ~100 positions x 15 length in numba ~2-4 min per fold; prefix MASS 5,326 queries x 0.19 s ~17 min for 1m (5m ~1 min). Total ~40-50 CPU-minutes for 1m, ~10 for 5m; peak memory under 400 MB (the 4,502^2 float32 distance matrix is 81 MB).
161	
162	**libraries.** numpy, scipy.signal.fftconvolve (MASS), numba (shapelet distances), sklearn (KMeans, AgglomerativeClustering, DecisionTreeClassifier), pandas.
163	
164	**output_as_config.** Two forms. Compact and preferred: scalar-feature rules (from the cluster-explaining tree or from the novelty deciles), e.g. {"if": [["nn_dist_prefix", ">", 4.2]], "then": "skip"} where nn_dist_prefix needs a small as-of routine (window length m, prefix MASS) added to the fz code under a config key {"novelty": {"window": 30, "skip_if_nn_dist_gt": 4.2}}. Alternative requiring a user decision: a shapelet template of <= 20 numbers plus a threshold {"shape_skip": {"template": [...], "max_dist": 1.8, "window": 30}}; a rule with a 20-number template is arguably compact but it is a new key type, so it is offered, not assumed.
165	
166	**novelty.** Matrix profile and MASS (Yeh et al. ICDM 2016; Mueen 2015; STOMP/SCRIMP 2017-2018), motif and discord discovery as the current standard for unsupervised pattern mining in long series; shapelets (Ye & Keogh 2009), learned/random shapelets (Grabocka et al. 2014; Karlsson et al. 2016 random shapelet forests); k-Shape and time-series clustering benchmarks (Paparrizos & Gravano 2015; Javed et al. 2020). The causal prefix-novelty score is a matrix-profile discord applied online.
167	
168	**Judge 1** feasible 4 · rigour 3 · expected value 1 · keep False — fix: Trap: 3,000 random shapelets x thresholds x ~30 clusters is a family 184 winners cannot pay for, every pre-SETUP path shares the engine's break-then-continue template, and a 20-number template as config is a new key type no practitioner would ship from this sample. Fix: compute only nn_dist_prefix and p1_dist_prefix (causal prefix MASS, ~17 minutes on 1m) as two scalar candidates for study 3; drop motif, cluster and shapelet search entirely.
169	
170	**Judge 2** feasible 4 · rigour 4 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: Z-normalised shape clusters and random shapelets on 15%-positive labels add ~3,000+ trials to the ledger with a low prior, and both deployable forms (20-number template, prefix-MASS routine) are new key types needing a user decision. Keep only the causal novelty scores nn_dist_prefix and p1_dist_prefix (prefix MASS, ~17 min on 1m, ~1 min on 5m, numba/fftconvolve present) as two candidate scalar features handed to the importance study; drop the motif and shapelet searches.
171	
172	### deep-sequence-pretrain-probe (priority 6)
173	
174	**technique.** Self-supervised representation learning on all IS bars, framework-free: a ladder of PCA (the linear autoencoder), an sklearn MLP bottleneck autoencoder, and a forecast-pretext encoder (predict the next 30-bar normalised path and realised range from the past 60), each followed by a linear probe on SETUP embeddings; the embedding is then clustered and the clusters distilled to rules.
175	
176	**what_it_answers.** Whether pretraining on the whole tape (445k 1m windows, most of them not SETUPs) yields a representation of the pre-SETUP window in which Foundation winners and losers are linearly separable better than in the raw features or the PCA baseline, i.e. whether the 'foundation-model' idea has any purchase at this scale without a deep-learning framework; and, if so, whether the useful directions can be named.

## 7. The card

One row per bar, computed as of that bar and never rewritten. Fields: `zone_id` (the ref band), `visit_n`, `this_bars`, `this_vol`, `vol_na`, `first_bars`, `first_vol`, `first_vol_na`, `read`, `left_id` (the band whose LEAVE is live), `out_run`, `out_side`, `session_bar`, `gap_pts`, `wick_depth`, `last_hunt_at/dir`, `last_reject_at/dir`, `cluster_sit`, `prev_bars`, `prev_vol`, `last_leave_failed`, `in_id` (the band containing the close, nearest mid), `leave_side`, `leave_vol_ok`, `leave_kind`, `first_clock_lived`.

**Read precedence.** LEAVE (a LEAVE is live on `left_id`) → HUNT → REJECT → the inside read of the ref band's visit when the close is inside it → PENDING (the close is outside the ref band, visit still live) → NEW (no ref band).

**Inside reads.** Visit 1 reads FIRST_PRINT (`first_clock_lived` says whether it has lasted `accept_bars`). On a revisit, with B = the base visit (`volume_base`: the first visit, or the previous one): ACCEPTED when `this_bars ≥ accept_bars` and (volume is NA on either side, or `this_vol ≥ accept_vol_ratio × B.vol`); else THIN when volume is live and `this_vol < thin_ratio × B.vol`; else RECYCLE.

**Volume NA.** A bar is NA when its session is not the front month (`front_month == 0` in the 1-minute file) or its volume is 0. A visit is NA if any of its bars is; the first visit's NA flag never changes. NA makes ACCEPTED time-only, THIN unavailable, the HUNT burst skipped and R4 skipped. Because `fm_na` folds the front-month flag in, two visits with live volume are always in the same volume regime, so a cross-regime ratio cannot be computed by construction.

`leave_vol_ok` (the R4 of a LEAVE read): per-bar mean volume of the far-side closes since R1 ≥ the sit's per-bar mean; `null` when either side is NA; re-evaluated on every far-side bar.

---

## 8. The gate at a Foundation SETUP

Evaluated on the SETUP bar k with direction S, after the watch step of that bar. The ledger row is created first with the card's columns; on a LEAVE read it also records the entered band (`entered_zone_id`, `entered_visit_n`, `entered_read` = that band's read as if it were the ref band).

1. **A REENTER already decided on this bar** by the watch step (R5 satisfied on the SETUP bar itself) makes the row `REENTER` with branch `watch`.
2. **Hard BLOCK**, in this order, no watch opened and any existing watch untouched: `in_position` (an FZ position is open on this bar), `clock` (bar open time ≥ `no_entry_from`), `open_pierce` (within the session's first `open_bars` bars and before `open_window_until`, the bar's range crosses an edge of a band whose last visit ended in an earlier session and that has fewer than `open_sit_closes` closes inside today), `hunt_fade` (the latest HUNT of the ref band or of the band just left, or of any band under `fade_scope = any_band`, is in S's direction, completed within `fade_block_bars`, same session), `new` (the read is NEW).
3. **TAKE branches**, the first that holds:
   - **leave**: read LEAVE, S equals the leave side, `leave_vol_ok` is not False, not a gap LEAVE inside the first `open_quiet_bars` bars, and `leave_far_side`: `any` accepts; `block_list` refuses when the entered band reads RECYCLE, THIN, HUNT or REJECT (`block_reason = leave_into_recycle`); `no_band` refuses whenever a band contains the close (`leave_into_band`). A refusal records `take_why` and falls through to WATCH.
   - **first_print**: read FIRST_PRINT, the visit is at least `first_print_min_bars` old, S equals the visit's `entry_dir`.
   - **defend**: read ACCEPTED and the ref band's latest HUNT or latest REJECT (one slot each, §6) fell in this visit, within `defend_window_bars`, at the edge S points away from.
   - A **leave** TAKE of the band a watch waits on, in the watch's direction, is that watch's REENTER instead (branch `leave`, `reenter_reason = take_on_watch:leave`); a first_print or defend TAKE stays Foundation's own position and leaves the watch as it is.
   - A TAKE calls `open_position('TAKE')`; the engine may have skipped the SETUP for a wrong-side stop, in which case the row records `refused` and no position opens. An opposite-direction TAKE ends an open watch (`opposite_take`). A converted (branch-1) REENTER that the callback refuses keeps `gate = REENTER` with `refused` set and no position, and its `outcome_gate` is then REENTER too; this has not occurred on the tape (0 rows in all four strategies), and what it should become is open (S44 b).
4. **WATCH_EDGE**: `edge_watch = ref_band`, the read is PENDING, the previous close was inside the ref band and S is the side the close is on: a watch on the ref band that is already armed (this bar is R1).
5. **WATCH**: a band contains the close: a watch on that band with `dir = S`, not armed.
6. **BLOCK `new`** otherwise.

One watch at a time: a later SETUP that opens a watch replaces the current one (`outcome = replaced`); a BLOCKed SETUP leaves it untouched. `gate` on the row is the decision as of the SETUP bar (what the truncation test compares); `outcome_gate` is how the SETUP ended (REENTER when a later REENTER used this SETUP as its R5), and the tables and headline counts use `outcome_gate`.

---

## 9. The watch machine

A watch pins a snapshot of its band (edges, mid, the sit's per-bar mean volume) and runs once per bar before the gate, from the bar after it opened.

- **Cancels**, checked first: the first bar of a new session (`session_end`); `leave_closes` consecutive closes beyond the band on the side opposite to the watch direction (`opposite_leave`); from ARMED, `cancel_inside_bars` consecutive closes back inside (`back_inside`). An opposite TAKE cancels from the gate (`opposite_take`).
- **R1**: a close beyond the band on the watch's side arms the watch (`armed_at`; `first_armed_at` on the first arming). A close back inside breaks the far-side run; the next far-side close arms again (R1 again), so R3 (no close inside or across the mid since R1) holds by construction on the unbroken run. The ledger reports both `armed_bars` (from the first arming) and `rearmed_bars` (from the latest).
- **R2**: `leave_closes` consecutive far-side closes. **R4**: per-bar mean volume of the far-side run ≥ the pinned sit mean, skipped (None) when the run or the sit is volume-NA. `r4_bars_evaluated / fail / na` are counted per window.
- **R5**: a Foundation SETUP in the watch direction on this bar or on the previous bar of the same session.
- **REENTER** on the first bar j where R1–R5 hold, unless the bar's open time is at or past `no_entry_from` (`clock_1520` counted, watch stays armed) or a position is open (`reenter_in_position`). The callback prices nothing back; it may refuse (`wrong_side_stop`, `sl_dead_at_fill`), counted as `reenter_refused`, the watch continues. On success the row of the R5 SETUP gets `fill_bar`, `fill_used` (`setup_close` when j is the SETUP bar, else `reenter_close`), `fill_delay_bars`, `edge_dist_pts`, `armed_bars`, `rearmed_bars`, `reenter_reason` and `outcome_gate = REENTER`.
- **Outcomes** in the watch log: `reenter`, `replaced`, `cancelled:<reason>` (never armed) or `armed_expired:<reason>` (armed), `active` at the data end. `no_same_dir_setup` counts armed watches that expired with R1–R4 satisfied on their last bar.

Position lifetime is entry bar ≤ k < exit bar, so a SETUP on a position's exit bar may open a new one at that bar's close; `build_trades` asserts that no two FZ positions overlap under that convention.

---

## 10. Execution: `fz_exec.py`

## 19. v2: rooms (Strategies 7, 8)

**Why.** The user's verdict on the base (2026-09-27): the card named tiles, not rooms. Zones were born at every protected level and every cluster sit, absorbed into a permanent 20-point mesh and never retired, so on 3 Sep the card said `B07-23 14:52 visit 7` (and `B07-02 10:31 visit 51` elsewhere) where the user saw one afternoon box; every LEAVE was a step from tile A into tile B; the first clock was a July sit, so the volume ratio was NA on the only window with volume; REENTER fired on tile edges. Median visit_n at a 1m SETUP was 19, FIRST_PRINT at SETUP 0, and the gate sat at the 6th percentile of its random control (S39). v2 changes identity only: what a room is, when it is born, when it dies, what it is called. Reads, precedence, PENDING, LEAVE liveness, REJECT, the gate's order and branches, `leave_far_side`, the watch machine, `fz_exec` and `fz_report` are the same code. Recorded as S42 in `docs/STRATEGY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`.

**Room model** (`room_model = "rooms"`, in `fz.py` next to the band model; `bands` is the base):

1. **Birth only from sits.** A room is born on the transition into a sit (the last `cluster_bars` closes of one session within `cluster_width`), centred on the sit's `(max + min) / 2`, ± `band_half_width`, origin = the sit's first bar; visit 1 is that sit, replayed over the window only. No drift births (`drift_birth = false`) and no swing births (`birth_a_source = "none"`; `protected_level` / `every_swing` still work in either model, as diagnostics).
2. **No mesh.** A sit overlapping a live room by at least `merge_overlap` of the width (with 0.5: its mid is inside the room) is a visit of that room, never a birth; it takes the live visit when its close is inside that room (below). Two live rooms never overlap (a shared edge is allowed). A sit that overlaps live rooms by less than `merge_overlap` is a new room, and `room_overlap` says how the overlap is removed: **`supersede`** (seeded): the new room keeps its full width and the rooms it overlaps are retired on its birth bar (`retired_by = superseded`); `clip`: the new room's edges stop at the neighbours' edges. Retired rooms absorb nothing and contain no price.
3. **Rooms retire.** On a session's first bar, a room with no inside close in the last `room_max_age_sessions` sessions (`session - last session with an inside close > room_max_age_sessions`) is retired (`retired_by = retired`), unless it holds the live visit. A new sit at a retired room's price is a new room with a new name and its own first clock. A LEAVE still live on a room that retires ends (`leave_end_retired`).
4. **Names.** `zone_id = "<letter> <mm-dd hh:mm>"`: the letter is the room's birth order within its birth session (A … Z, then AA, AB …), the time its birth bar. Rooms keep `kind = "B"` (sit-born; `A` only under a swing `birth_a_source`), so the Zone-gate tab's zone-kind table and the chart colours work unchanged.
5. **Visits and touches.** A stay with fewer than `visit_min_bars` inside closes that ends by the leave rule is a *touch*: it keeps its record (`touch: true`), does not advance `visit_n`, and is counted on the room and on the card (`touches`). Visit numbers are as-of: the current stay counts as a visit while it lasts. The first visit (`first_bars`, `first_vol`) and the previous visit (`volume_base = previous`, `prev_bars`) are the first / previous stay that is not a touch. With `visit_min_bars = 1` no stay can be a touch (a stay opens on an inside close), which is how the base stays unchanged.
6. **The live visit follows the sit.** When a room is born, or a sit is absorbed by a live room, while another room holds the live visit and the sit's close is inside the new (or absorbing) room, the old visit ends at the previous bar (`ended_by = sit_moved`, no LEAVE is recorded) and the room the market sits in takes the visit (the base instead cuts the newborn zone's replayed visit, `ref_live`). A room retired by supersession while it holds the visit with no room taking over ends its visit with `ended_by = superseded`.
7. **Leave and hunt.** `leave_closes` 1m 3, 5m 2 (so HUNT and LEAVE do not overlap on 1m). The close-form HUNT is `1 ≤ outside run ≤ hunt_max_bars` closes on one side, then a close back inside (the base only ever had a run of 1); the burst test takes the loudest of those outside bars and is skipped when any of them is volume-NA (identical to the base for a run of 1). The 5m wick form is unchanged.
8. **First clock and volume** come from visit 1 of this room, born in the memory horizon, so on the Design window they are live; NA handling is unchanged.

**Keys** (all four files carry all of them; the base values keep Strategies 5 and 6 unchanged, source `evaluation:v2 (base model, no behaviour change)`):

**`room_overlap` is a build choice, not in the plan.** The plan says both "a sit overlapping a live room by less than `merge_overlap` is a new room" and "two live rooms never overlap", which contradict each other for a partial overlap. The first build clipped (`clip`): on 1m it clipped 131 of 226 rooms and left slivers (on 2 Sep `D 09-02 12:45` was 0.65 points wide, `F 09-02 14:38` 10.25), and on 3 Sep the afternoon box was split between two 2 Sep fragments with a 13-visit neighbour: the 10-point stagger the verdict rejects. `supersede` keeps every room the width and mid of a real sit. The cost is memory: a room superseded by a partly overlapping sit is gone even if price later returns to it. Both options stay in code; `clip` is the named alternative and is never seeded.

**User decisions 2026-09-27 (after the first acceptance run).** (1) Room E (`E 09-03 12:20 · 24029.5–24049.5`) is the 3 Sep noon room; F must not exist; E is not widened toward 24000 (23985 is the poke under the room, not the room); existing rooms' edges are never touched. The 13:48 sit (mid 24018) that was F is kept by `B 09-02 10:30 · 23999.3–24019.3`, also crossed that session. The window then reads `D 09-02 14:38` visits 4–9 and `B 09-02 10:30` visits 13–14 (two-digit), no room born on 3 Sep after 09:48, and the 13:11 up / 13:23 down SETUPs still gate TAKE on branch defend (on D 09-02 visit 5). Note also that the 13:48 sit's band (24008–24028) does not overlap E's (24029.5–24049.5) at all, so call 2 alone could not have removed F even if E had been born. Card statistics under call 2 (ST7 / ST8, All data): 2.0 / 1.8 rooms born per session, 61.5% / 55.4% of bars inside a room, NEW 6.2% / 9.8%, LEAVE 42.4% / 32.8%, visit_n at SETUP median 9.5 (max 27) / 5 (max 17). The "First numbers" and first "Priced" tables below are from the build before call 2 (`same_session_overlap` absent, i.e. `supersede`). The lab *was* then run under the call-2 seeds: the stored ST7 / ST8 results (filtered run, 2026-09-27 19:57–20:00) and the published `results/summary.json` / `dashboard.html` (plain run, 21:01, committed in `8761709`) carry the call-2 numbers in the last table of this section; their cache keys match the files and code on disk.

**User decisions 2026-09-28 (the three identity questions).** (1) `session_visit_rule` (`any_close` | `sit`, seeded `sit`): "visited this session" for `keep_older` means a real sit today, a run of at least `cluster_bars` consecutive same-session closes inside the room (the sit that bore the room counts), not any close. Order in `room_fit`: `merge_overlap` absorption, then `keep_older`, then `adjacent_birth`, then `room_overlap`. Strategies 5 and 6 unchanged bit for bit (pre-v2 snapshot, all fields).

408	    for name, Lv in (("prot", p), ("room", Lr), ("swing", Ls)):
409	        ne, verdict, ago = touch_stats(Lv, k)
410	        f.update({f"touch_{name}_n": ne, f"touch_{name}_last": verdict, f"touch_{name}_bars_ago": ago})
